body: I get a 404 when opening the link you sent by email. Could you please send a new link and update this issue when you have done it?

I can see this issue as well after upgrading from 2.11.5 to 2.12.1. The issue is only noticed when actually using a ffmpeg audio track and then switching text track. If I were to play a stream which is supported by my device (and ffmpeg is not needed) I do not see this issue.
Is this issue being looked at? It really makes an upgrade impossible.

Yes. This is a fairly obscure issue where `MediaCodecAudioRenderer` (which is not being used) inadvertently resets the state of the `AudioSink` that's shared across all of the audio renderers.

As a workaround, you can implement an `RenderersFactory` to provide each audio renderer with its own `AudioSink`, rather than doing what `DefaultRenderersFactory` is doing and sharing a single instance.

I got a few class names wrong in my response above, so it didn't make much sense. I've updated it to be correct now (if reading by email, please open the thread on GitHub to see the correct version). Thanks!

Thank you for your answer. I was just composing my answer with a question if you meant `RenderersFactory` and not `ExtractorsFactory`.
The workaround is working.

This is fixed by the change ref'd above. We'll include this in `2.12.2`, which is due in the next couple of weeks. Note that:

1. Once using `2.12.2`, the workaround will be unnecessary.
1. We didn't fix this by having each renderer use its own `AudioSink`. Instead, we fixed the problem that was causing sharing of the `AudioSink` to not work.

issue.title: Change/disable subtitle track with ffmpeg enabled stops playback

repository.name: ExoPlayer
repository.description: This project is deprecated and stale. The latest ExoPlayer code is available in https://github.com/androidx/media

issue.body:
###  Issue description
If ffmpeg is enabled and currently being used for audio decoding, when you change or disable (or enable) subtitle tracks, playback stops, but it doesn't pause or stop the video (Exoplayer thinks it's still playing, but video & audio do not progress.

### Reproduction steps
This code from TrackSelectionDialogBuilder:
```
            trackSelector.setParameters(
                TrackSelectionUtil.updateParametersWithOverride(
                    selectionParameters,
                    rendererIndex,
                    rendererTrackGroups,
                    newIsDisabled,
                    newOverrides.isEmpty() ? null : newOverrides.get(0)));
```
Causes the error if
`RendersFactory rendersFactory = new DefaultRenderersFactory(getActivity()).setExtensionRendererMode(DefaultRenderersFactory.EXTENSION_RENDERER_MODE_PREFER)`
is used 100% of the time.

If
`RendersFactory rendersFactory = new DefaultRenderersFactory(getActivity()).setExtensionRendererMode(DefaultRenderersFactory.EXTENSION_RENDERER_MODE_ON)`
is used, then the problem only surfaces if ffmpeg is used as a fallback

I don't know if this is an ffmpeg issue, or if it's something with the way that Exoplayer is processing the override. I should note that overriding the audio does not cause playback to stop.
There are no messages in the debug log to indicate that an error occured.

ffmpeg was compiled with all the codecs supported by Exoplayer (per the documentation of supported formats)

### Link to test content
n/a - should be reproducible with any internet stream when using ffmpeg to decode audio

### A full bug report captured from the device
n/a

### Version of ExoPlayer being used
Exoplayer 2.12.1, ffmpeg 4.2 and 4.3 both tried.

### Device(s) and version(s) of Android being used
It seems to happen on all devices where the ffmpeg codec is currently being used to decode audio. I've tested on Tivo Stream 4k (API 28), Fire Stick 4k (API 25), Android Emulator with Android TV builds, APIs 26, 27, 28, 30.
